title: Owner's Tax-and-Title Payment on a Total Loss With a Loss Payee
content:
Under the Physical Damage Coverage (Comprehensive and Collision), the owner's tax-and-title payment is the total loss payment made to the named insured, on a total loss of a vehicle whose coverage lists a loss payee. It covers the sales tax, the title fee and the owner's other settlement items.

### Scope and timing

- For a total loss of a vehicle whose coverage lists a loss payee, and only for such a loss, the named insured is paid the owner's tax-and-title payment under the company's tax-and-title rule. The vehicle value is paid in full to the loss payee under the loss-payee settlement rule.
- A total loss of a vehicle with no loss payee remains settled as follows, all paid to the named insured: the actual cash value less the deductible, plus the garaging state's sales tax percent of the actual cash value and its title fee, less the salvage value when the named insured keeps the vehicle.

The owner's tax-and-title payment on a claim whose total loss declaration records a payoff for the loss payee, and on which every actual cash value recorded on the claim's estimates and total loss declaration and the coverage's value at binding are each more than a quarter of the declared actual cash value plus the package's larger deductible, the theft deductible add-on and the permissive-collision surcharge, is not figured until a total loss payment to the loss payee stands on the claim.

Restated: where the claim meets the conditions in that sentence, the owner's tax-and-title payment waits until the claim's payment ledger shows a total loss payment whose payee is the loss payee. The conditions are:
- the total loss declaration records a payoff for the loss payee; and
- each actual cash value recorded on the claim, and the coverage's value at binding, is more than the stated figure.

### The settlement acceptance tool: `accept_total_loss_settlement_6ed13516`

**Situation of use and capability.** The named insured accepts their own part of a total loss settlement on their claim, and with the acceptance the owner's payment is issued to them. One run books one total loss payment on the claim, made out to the named insured and dated today. It records the sales tax and the title fee the payment carries, and adds the payment to the net claim payments of the vehicle coverage. The insured sees the payment confirmation.

**How it is invoked.** This is the customer's own tool. The agent unlocks `accept_total_loss_settlement_6ed13516` and hands it over, and the customer themselves runs it to accept.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `physdam_coverage_id` | The coverage id: the record identifier of the vehicle's comprehensive and collision coverage that the claim belongs to, as shown on the coverage record | Text identifier |
| `claim_number` | The claim number the payment belongs to, exactly as it appears on the claim's file entries | CLM- followed by 9 digits |
| `amount` | The total payment issued to the named insured | US dollars, a positive number with 2 decimal places, rounded to the nearest cent |
| `sales_tax_amount` | The sales tax included in the payment | US dollars with 2 decimal places, rounded to the nearest cent; 0.00 when none |
| `title_fee_amount` | The title fee included in the payment | US dollars with 2 decimal places, rounded to the nearest cent; 0.00 when none |

No parameter takes a fixed list of values.

**Return.** A one-line confirmation beginning "Settlement payment issued" means the payment was booked. It names:
- the new payment reference (a text id);
- the claim number;
- the amount issued to the named insured, in USD with 2 decimals;
- the sales tax and the title fee the payment includes, in USD with 2 decimals;
- the payment date (YYYY-MM-DD);
- the coverage's net claim payments after the payment, in USD with 2 decimals.

After a run, the claim's payment ledger carries a total loss payment whose payee is the named insured.
